newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-CABINET TO DECIDE ON BUTINGE CREDITS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-CABINET TO DECIDE ON BUTINGE CREDITS.

text.p: The Lithuanian government is to decide on Wednesday to ask for parliament's urgent approval to issue state guarantee for credits worth $200 million from six foreign banks to finance building the Butinge oil terminal.
Financing the planned terminal has been a headache for the government as some backers have agreed to fund it and then dropped out.
The foreign loans commission has already backed a plan to issue guarantees to six banks including Union Bank of Switzerland (US affiliate) and U.S. EXIM Bank.
Sources in the government told Reuters that the cabinet might decide to reduce the sum suggested by the loans commission for state guarantees to $100 million.
The finance ministry said in a statement that the construction of Butinge oil terminal needs around $202 million and the banks have offered a total of $260 million in credits.
The ministry also said concrete credit sums from each bank and the terms should be established when signing the contracts.
Some $65 million of the funds will be from Lithuania. The ministry said 96.7 million litas was invested in construction of the terminal, 60.9 million litas of it from the budget.
The current share capital of Butinge oil terminal stands at 71.26 million litas and 85.52 percent of it is state run.
The shareholders of Butinge decided in March to boost the sharecapital to 260 million litas and the state has acquired shares worth 28 million litas already.
Parliament has decided that the state's stake in the company should be no less than 34 percent and any single investor can own no more than 33 percent stake in the firm.
